MarketScreener's profile returned 403. Do not quote 777 as group headcount.
vendors.hardware_track_record: About 34 years of display manufacturing and 17 as the consolidated ePaper group. Prime View International founded 1992 as Taiwan's first TFT LCD company; E Ink Corporation spun out of the MIT Media Lab in 1997; Prime View acquired E Ink Corporation in 2009 (reported consideration about US$215 million) and rebranded; also acquired Hydis Technologies (2008) and SiPix Technology (December 2012). LARGE-FORMAT IS BEING BUILT OUT RIGHT NOW, which is the single most reassuring fact for this buyer: the H5 line entered volume production in late 2025 producing 32-inch and 55-inch signage panels; an H6 line launches in 2026 at Hsinchu Science Park with revenue expected in 2027; plus the Taoyuan Guanyin site and stated US capacity increases. A 75-inch Spectra 6 module was announced 2025-04-10 with Q4 2025 partner samples, following a 75-inch Kaleido 3 earlier that year. CEO Johnson Lee: the company 'continues to prioritize larger formats across its ePaper portfolio' and 'I am bullish about this market, so we have to keep expanding capacity.' In April 2025 E Ink signed a term sheet for a JV with AUO Display Plus (ADP 51% / E Ink 49%, NT$390 million paid-in capital) for large-sized EPD module lines at AUO's Longke site in Taoyuan, mass production from Q4 2025, explicitly to 'establish a comprehensive and reliable large-sized ePaper supply chain'. Named large-format ecosystem partners: Sharp (ePoster), PPDS (Philips Tableaux), StellarLink, Hanshow; silicon partners Himax, Realtek, MediaTek. E Ink also sells >=15in modules directly through its own shopkits store: 25.3in Spectra 3100 ($1,400), 25.3in Spectra 6 ($1,400), 31.5in Spectra 6 (out of stock), 25.3in Kaleido 3.
vendors.abandonment_history: MATERIAL, AND A FRAME BUYER SHOULD READ THIS TWICE. (1) PANEL GENERATIONS. E Ink spent, by one industry account, over US$100 million developing Gallery 3 (ACeP) for e-readers, shipped it in essentially one size — 8 inches — never scaled it up or down, then dropped it from its stated 2024 focus, which named only Kaleido 3, Outdoor Kaleido 3 and Spectra 6. EOL notices were issued for certain ACeP-based products in early 2024 and the Bigme Galy was discontinued. Only two brands ever shipped a Gallery 3 device; PocketBook's planned Viva slipped repeatedly. The same account notes E Ink 'lacks documentation' — no white papers or tutorials for solving the panel's responsiveness — pushing the integration burden onto device makers and killing adoption. (2) SUBSIDIARIES. E Ink acquired Hydis Technologies in 2008 and, as largest shareholder, called for a halt to Korean factory operations in January 2015, telling Korean government agencies it would close the factories and discontinue production. Local critics said E Ink bought Hydis for its FFS technology without meaningful capital investment; the Korean Metal Workers Union pursued the matter through an OECD national contact point. (3) ITS OWN CYCLICAL FRAGILITY. E Ink reported a 46% YoY sales drop and a US$33.6 million net loss in 2013 (biggest in four years) when e-reader demand collapsed, and a Q1 2014 net loss of NT$603 million on an operating loss of NT$1.21 billion with revenue of NT$2.96 billion. It is a far stronger business now, but the record shows it cuts a product line hard when the economics turn.
vendors.distributor_footprint: Sells modules to OEMs under negotiated MOQ; runs its own shopkits webshop for kits and small buyers, which also carries partner products such as the Digital View 32in outdoor display. Does not sell to individuals or hobbyists.
vendors.rationale: As a going concern E Ink is the safest name in this survey by a wide margin: listed, profitable, net-cash, 30% net margins, 55% gross margin, 18% ROE, paying a dividend, and guiding capex UP to NT$5-8bn in 2026 specifically to add large-format capacity. Its position is a near-monopoly — one independent analysis calls it 'a global monopoly in the production of e-paper display panels', and the trade press argues its core electrophoretic patent expired in 2017 but the group had already acquired its main competitors, leaving 'no real competition in the ereader and eNote space'. Corroborating that from the downstream side: this survey found only one credible technological challenger, CLEARINK, and it has been dark since mid-2020. WHAT THE DEPENDENCY MEANS FOR SOMEONE BUYING A FRAME TODAY, concretely: (a) SINGLE POINT OF FAILURE ON PANEL GENERATION. Every colour art frame here runs one of two E Ink colour families and the large ones are all Spectra 6. If Spectra 6 went the way of Gallery 3, no downstream vendor has a second source — there is no second electrophoretic foundry. Judge a frame by whether its panel generation is one E Ink is investing behind. Right now the evidence is good: H5 is in volume production for 32in and 55in, H6 and Guanyin are funded, and a 75in Spectra 6 module has partner samples. Spectra 6 is the generation E Ink is scaling, not stranding. Kaleido 3 (the panel in every 25.3in monitor here) is also still in E Ink's stated focus list — but it is the older, weaker-colour technology and is the more likely of the two to be deprioritised first. (b) PANEL SUPPLY IS ALLOCATED, NOT MERCHANDISED. E Ink's own FAQ states it does not sell to individual consumers or small hobbyists, gives no free samples, and negotiates MOQ case by case by size and custom-vs-standard; individuals are pointed at the shopkits webshop. A small frame brand has no contractual claim on supply, and in an allocation-tight period — ESL volumes of 500m units in 2025 heading to 600m in 2026 utterly dwarf the art-frame market — a boutique frame maker is the customer E Ink can most cheaply disappoint. (c) SPARE PANELS FOR WARRANTY REPAIR ARE THE PRACTICAL FAILURE MODE. When a small vendor folds or loses allocation, a cracked 40-inch Spectra 6 panel becomes unobtainable at any price, because the buyer cannot go to E Ink directly. (d) TWO STRUCTURAL IMPROVEMENTS IN THE BUYER'S FAVOUR. First, the AUO JV industrialises large-format module assembly at a listed panel maker with real capacity, making 30-40in modules more commodity-like over time. Second, E Ink is taking equity in its own customers — it is a shareholder in Onyx International via Onyx's 2025 Series B — which aligns panel supply with specific device makers' survival. Onyx is the only device vendor in this survey with the panel monopolist on its cap table, and that is a genuine differentiator. (e) PRACTICAL HEDGE. Prefer a device whose image path is a documented local interface (USB, SD, HDMI, local network push) over one whose value depends on a vendor cloud or subscription, because E Ink-driven panel decisions will outlast any given brand's servers.

vendors.corporate_form: Early-stage private company; no legal entity form disclosed on any page fetched

vendors.funding: Crowdfunding only, as far as can be established. Kickstarter raised USD 1,120,290 from 1,825 backers against a USD 10,000 goal, campaign 2025-09-23 to 2025-10-23. No investors disclosed. The campaign was professionally promoted by Jellop, an ad-tech agency associated with 3,500+ successful Kickstarter projects, and showcased on BackerClub - so the raise reflects paid marketing amplification as much as organic demand.
vendors.revenue_scale: Approximately USD 1.1M crowdfunding plus subsequent direct sales; both SKUs are currently sold out, so DTC revenue is not estimable.
vendors.headcount: Not disclosed. Described only as a team with 'a combined 30+ years of product design and development experience' across automotive, manufacturing, consumer electronics, cloud computing and wireless communication - phrasing that typically indicates a very small team.
vendors.hardware_track_record: ONE PRODUCT, NOT YET DELIVERED AT SCALE. The founder does have prior hardware crowdfunding experience through Hooke Audio, which ran two campaigns (Hooke Verse binaural headphones and Hooke Lav, which hit its $10,000 goal with $100,000 in eight hours); both delivered, with pandemic-era parts delays on the Lav. Fraimic itself has no shipping history. Manufacturing is contracted to Sungale Electronics — Fraimic designs and brands, it does not manufacture. Products: Standard Canvas 13.3in at $399 and Large Canvas 31.5in at $999, both Spectra 6; only the 31.5in is in scope. Won a Red Dot Product Design award in 2026.
vendors.abandonment_history: No abandonment yet, but an ACTIVE AND DOCUMENTED FULFILMENT SLIP. Backers were promised May 2026 and DTC June 2026. A campaign-analysis service fetched 2026-08-05 reports that as of 2026-07-27 there was no public confirmation any backer had received a unit; that a mid-May pre-production review said full launch had moved to June 2026, implying mass production had not started on time; that the Large Canvas list price had risen roughly 50% from the planned $999 to about $1,499; and that the pre-production unit shipped with software bugs. Mitigating signals in the same analysis: a CES 2026 prototype demo, a named manufacturing partner, a functioning retail store with inventory movement, and a creator update dated 2026-07-21 — so this reads as late, not absconded. Overall trust score 75/100 (medium-low), flagged as a first-time hardware creator with unresolved fulfilment uncertainty. ONE UNVERIFIED LEAD THAT WOULD CHANGE THE RATING: reports that Hooke Audio was acquired by Logitech in 2021 and that the Hooke app was pulled from the App Store, functionally stranding Verse owners. If true, that is a direct precedent for exactly the abandonment the client is screening for and would move Fraimic to a firm low. I could not fetch a working source.
vendors.rationale: One-product startup, first hardware, single crowdfunding round, no disclosed institutional investment, founder-led, small team. Say it plainly: there is no financial buffer visible here and no second product line to fall back on. The mitigating evidence is real but limited - they have actually shipped the smaller SKU and physically landed the larger one, which puts them ahead of most Kickstarter hardware, and the raise was 112x the goal so there was cash to execute with. Against them, the product's core differentiator (Voice-to-Vision AI generation) depends on vendor-side AI infrastructure and purchasable AI credits, which is an ongoing operating cost that must be funded indefinitely; if the company stops paying for it, the marquee feature dies even if the frame keeps working. For this client that dependency is largely irrelevant since he would not use AI generation - but it is the thing most likely to consume the company's cash. Critically, unlike Modos, nothing is open: no schematics, no SDK, no published local protocol, so company failure would leave the client with an undocumented device and a browser-upload path that may or may not keep functioning. The advertised local-only mode is the one thing that would survive a vendor shutdown, and it is undocumented enough that this cannot be relied on.

vendors.hardware_track_record: The longest hardware track record of any non-panel-maker in this slice: 'over 27 Years of Experience in ARM Embedded Design and Manufacturing', with its own production factory. Six product lines spanning Edge AI hardware, ARM System-on-Modules (NXP, Rockchip, Renesas, MediaTek, Qualcomm), single-board computers, industrial embedded systems and mini PCs, e-paper displays and signage, and IoT gateways. Semiconductor partnerships shown with NXP, Hailo, Rockchip and Renesas. vendors.abandonment_history: Not investigated; nothing found.
vendors.rationale: Rated medium and arguably the most interesting durability profile in this slice. The positives are substantial and unusual here: 27 years of continuous ARM embedded design and manufacturing, an owned 30,000+ sq m factory, 100+ R&D engineers, 2,000+ claimed clients, tier-one silicon partnerships, and six diversified product lines - so e-paper signage failing would not take the company with it, unlike every startup in this survey where the frame IS the company. Not rated high because nothing is independently verifiable: no public financials, no ticker, no disclosed ownership, headcount and factory figures are self-reported marketing claims, and their about-us page was not retrievable (404) so the corporate detail rests on the homepage alone. For a private buyer there is also a practical durability caveat distinct from corporate survival - this is a B2B ODM/OEM supplier, so consumer-style warranty, spares and support over a decade should not be assumed, and MOQ friction is likely. WHY IT MATTERS ANYWAY: Geniatech is the only vendor in this survey that combines credible corporate durability with an Android 11 applications processor, an in-house TCON, an explicitly 'Open API & SDK', and all three of the interesting panel sizes including the 163 PPI 25.3 in. On the two criteria jointly it may be the best available compromise, and it is the single vendor most worth a direct commercial enquiry.

vendors.name: Modos Tech Inc (out of scope on size — included because its licensing model inverts the whole risk analysis)
vendors.corporate_form: Incorporated company with TWO PEOPLE IN IT: Alexander Soto (founder/CEO) and Wenting Zhang (co-founder, FPGA/gateware engineer). Not a one-person project, but two is not an engineering organisation.
vendors.ownership: Founder-held
vendors.funding: NO VC. Partial development funding for the Caster display controller from the NLnet Foundation / NGI0 Entrust Fund (European Commission Next Generation Internet programme), plus enrolment in AMD's FPGA Playground. Revenue is crowdfunding pre-sales: the Modos Paper Monitor / Paper Dev Kit raised US$197,588 against a US$110,000 goal (179%) from 422 backers, funded 2025-09-18.

vendors.hardware_track_record: About one year of shipping. MAXIMUM PANEL IS 13.3IN — the Glider Mega Adapter spans 4.3in to 13.3in, the compatible-panel list tops out at 13.3in, and Modos Flow is 13.3in. There is no larger product announced or hinted. MODOS DOES NOT BELONG IN A >15IN SHORTLIST. Delivery record: shipping was originally expected January 2026; first shipment was still only 'starting soon' in February 2026, with a further update 2026-04-01 on shipping, cases and firmware. A prior product FAILED OUTRIGHT — the Modos Paper Laptop, announced January 2022, never reached production due to manufacturing and sourcing challenges (the 2022 plan was a 25-50 unit community pilot on rebuilt Lenovo ThinkPad T42 chassis, gated on a survey seeking about 50,000 respondents). They also opened a SECOND campaign before finishing the first: Modos Flow launched about 2026-05-27 at 13.3in, 3200x2400, $619 mono / $719 colour on a $150,000 target with delivery 'by mid-December 2026', while Paper Monitor units were still going out.
vendors.abandonment_history: One dead prior product (Paper Laptop) and a moderate slip on the current one. No orphaned firmware — but only because there is barely any installed base yet. Note that Modos does not run its own fulfilment, support desk or RMA: 'Produced by Modos Tech in Boston, MA. Sold and shipped by Crowd Supply' (Portland, Oregon). No distributor, no Amazon, no B&H.
vendors.distributor_footprint: Crowd Supply only
vendors.rationale: Blunt: a two-person open-hardware project with one dead prior product, about US$198,000 of lifetime revenue, no VC, an EU research grant, no warehouse, no support organisation, and nothing in the client's size class. On corporate survival the honest answer is probably not, and it does not matter, because they do not sell what he is buying. BUT THERE IS ONE GENUINE COUNTERPOINT THAT INVERTS THE USUAL LOGIC AND THE CLIENT SHOULD TAKE IT SERIOUSLY AS A PRINCIPLE: everything Modos makes is open hardware and open source — Caster gateway, firmware, schematics, C API and issue tracker all public on GitHub. If Modos Tech dissolves tomorrow, the firmware remains buildable and maintainable by third parties. That is the exact opposite of the Onyx profile, where the company is durable but the firmware is a black box with no source rights. For a buyer whose real requirement is 'will firmware still work in three years', Modos is the only vendor here where corporate death does not imply firmware death. It just cannot sell him a 25-inch panel. The transferable lesson: source availability is a substitute for corporate longevity, and it is worth asking every vendor whether any part of the stack is open.

vendors.funding: Deliberately not venture-funded - IEEE Spectrum reports the team 'emphasizes community-driven development rather than venture capital'. vendors.hardware_track_record: One product designed, manufactured and shipped: the Paper Dev Kit, funded September 2025, first shipment starting February 2026, with shipping/case/firmware progress updates through April 2026 and the 13 in kit now marked In stock. Certifications completed. A second product (Flow) has passed pre-production revisions with validation and testing done, contract manufacturers in China contracted, full BoM, supplier quotes and tooling in place, panels sourced directly from E Ink, and fulfilment via Crowd Supply's partner Mouser Electronics. The opposite pattern is evidenced: 11 public updates on campaign 1 including post-delivery firmware progress, 7 on campaign 2, a public issue tracker, published changelogs and versioned firmware releases. Their own risk statement concedes that development timelines typically need doubling, and delivery did run from a September 2025 funding to a February 2026 first shipment.
vendors.rationale: BLUNT ASSESSMENT: this is a two-person company with under USD 1M of lifetime crowdfunding revenue, no institutional investment, a grant from a public-interest fund, and exactly one product delivered to date. On a three-year horizon the probability that Modos Tech still exists as a going concern is materially below that of any incorporated competitor here, and the client should not plan a hardware dependency on the company continuing. HOWEVER - and this is the case the brief asked to be made explicitly - the staying-power question is much less damaging for Modos than for any other low-durability vendor in this survey, because everything that matters is already published under open licences: Caster gateware under CERN-OHL-P, Glider hardware under CERN-OHL-S, firmware under MIT, a host API with Python/Rust/C bindings, full schematics and design files, and 2.5k GitHub stars on Glider with 301 on Caster. If Modos folds tomorrow, the design survives and remains buildable and maintainable by third parties. That is the precise inverse of the InkPoster or Samsung risk profile, where the company will very likely persist but the device is unmaintainable by anyone outside it. Modos wins criterion 2 outright and loses criterion 1 outright, and the openness genuinely mitigates the corporate fragility in a way it does not for anyone else here.

vendors.funding: No equity funding. Grant plus crowdfunding: a Crowd Supply campaign against a $110,000 goal (press reported it raised nearly double), and an NLnet grant under NGI0 Entrust for the Caster controller project (amount not published; reported grant period Oct 2022 - Jan 2026, which I did not verify myself).
vendors.revenue_scale: Pre-revenue to minimal — crowdfunding stage
vendors.headcount: TWO PEOPLE. IEEE Spectrum describes Modos as 'a two-person startup with open-hardware roots', naming cofounders Alexander Soto and Wenting Zhang.
vendors.hardware_track_record: Short and unproven as a shipper, strong as an engineering project. Glider and Caster are fully published — KiCad hardware, STM32H750 firmware, FPGA gateware, extensive documentation — with 2.5k GitHub stars and 166 commits, and coverage in IEEE Spectrum, Hackaday, CNX Software and Notebookcheck. The technical claim is real and verified: 75 Hz on e-paper against a typical ~10 Hz, achieved by treating each pixel individually rather than the panel as a whole.
vendors.abandonment_history: A DOCUMENTED PATTERN OF ANNOUNCE-THEN-SLIP, WITH ONE LINE ABANDONED. Modos announced an E Ink laptop in early 2022, pivoted in early 2024 to the Paper Monitor as 'a more reasonable goal', then published a roadmap in late December 2024 claiming a Crowd Supply campaign would launch in February 2025. It did not. By April 2025 Good e-Reader wrote that neither product would be released, that only one update had been posted, and called Modos 'a cautionary tale when a company with no history of making consumer products makes news on all tech blogs with grand ambitions and no follow-through'. To be fair to Modos, that obituary was premature: the campaign DID launch about five months late, with a crowdfunding deadline of 2025-09-18, but as a bare developer kit (panel plus logic board, enclosure excluded) rather than the consumer monitor. Shipping then moved again — January 2026 expected, later coverage indicating July 2026 — and I could not verify current status because crowdsupply.com returned HTTP 403 on every attempt.
vendors.rationale: Two people, no equity investor, one product line abandoned at prototype, a campaign that slipped roughly five months and shipped as a bare dev kit, and ship dates that have moved at least twice since. There is no organisation behind a warranty or a firmware commitment. On conventional criteria this is the least durable vendor in the survey and must not be a sole dependency. BUT the usual conclusion does not follow, and this is the one place where 'low staying power' should not end the conversation: the hardware is KiCad, the firmware and FPGA gateware are published under open licences, and the design is mirrored across GitHub and GitLab. If Modos folds he still has schematics, gateware and a driveable controller — more continuity than a solvent vendor with locked firmware would give him. Rated low on the company; noted as the highest-optionality technical path here.

vendors.name: Onyx International / Boox (Guangzhou Onyx Technology Co., Ltd.)
vendors.corporate_form: Private limited company, established 2008-12-16. Chinese name 广州文石信息科技有限公司. Trades to Western customers as Onyx International.
vendors.ownership: Private, founder-led: co-founders Dan Yuting (chairwoman) and Zhu Zeng (CEO), plus institutional investors from the 2025 Series B.
vendors.funding: Series B in 2025 of 'tens of millions of USD' at a valuation in the hundreds of millions of yuan. INVESTORS ARE THE HEADLINE: Lenovo Capital & Incubator Group, E INK HOLDINGS INC., and Cedarview Capital Management.
vendors.revenue_scale: Not disclosed
vendors.hardware_track_record: About 15-17 years: Boox A60 e-reader in 2009, Boox M92 in November 2011, Android-based devices from 2013 onward, and one of the broadest current e-paper product ranges in the industry. >15in products: Mira Pro 25.3in (launched late 2023) and Mira Pro Color 25.3in (3200x1800 Kaleido 3, $1,899, announced 2025-04-28), shipped from a Hong Kong warehouse. 1-year warranty on core devices, 2 years via the Euro Shop.
vendors.abandonment_history: TWO SERIOUS, DOCUMENTED PROBLEMS. (1) GPL NON-COMPLIANCE, UNRESOLVED. As of 2022 Onyx DECLINED to release its Linux kernel modifications under GPLv2 in response to a written user request. A complaint was filed on the company forum 2018-10-19 (archived 2022-01-09) and escalated publicly to Hacker News on 2020-07-05 ('Onyx is violating the Linux kernel's license, refuses to release source code', 326 points). No resolution is documented. THE PROCUREMENT CONSEQUENCE IS THE POINT: if Onyx drops a model there is no legal source drop and therefore NO COMMUNITY-FIRMWARE FALLBACK — the device is exactly as dead as Onyx decides it is. (2) A STATED THREE-YEAR FIRMWARE FLOOR, WHICH CUTS BOTH WAYS: Onyx commits to 'free firmware updates for all models for at least three years after the product's launch'. That is unusually explicit and honest — but the client's horizon is three years, so buying an in-market SKU that launched in 2023 (the original Mira Pro) means the committed window may already be expiring. (3) A CONCRETE ABANDONMENT INSTANCE: the Boox Note Max (13.3in) was discontinued 2026-02-07 with defects still unresolved — 'issues with ghosting in PDF files and during internet browsing. Various firmware updates haven't resolved the issue.' Discontinued rather than fixed. Also reported: removal of the built-in app store and cessation of package/manual/changelog renewals on the downloads site from 2023-01-01 (unverified). No layoffs, insolvency or acquisitions found.
vendors.distributor_footprint: The broadest first-party footprint in the device set: own store shipping to US, UK, EU, Norway, Switzerland, Canada, Australia, Japan, Taiwan, Gulf states and Southeast Asia, with CE/RoHS/FCC/PSE certification.
vendors.rationale: The best-capitalised, longest-shipping, best-distributed China-side vendor, and the ONLY device vendor in this entire survey with the panel monopolist on its cap table — E Ink Holdings is an equity investor via the 2025 Series B, alongside Lenovo Capital. That is the strongest panel-supply-continuity signal available anywhere here, and it is worth more to a three-year horizon than any amount of marketing. The company will exist in three years. THE RISK IS NOT CORPORATE FRAGILITY, IT IS FIRMWARE POSTURE: Onyx has demonstrated it will discontinue a buggy model rather than fix it, and its refusal to honour GPL removes the escape hatch that would otherwise let a community keep the device alive. For this client specifically there is also a strong practical argument: the Mira Pro Color is a plain HDMI/USB-C monitor, so his app simply renders to it with no cloud, no account and no vendor app in the path — architecturally the cleanest large-format option in the survey. The offsetting art-specific problem is the panel: Kaleido 3 is a colour-filter technology over a monochrome panel with only 4,096 colours, noticeably desaturated and darker than Spectra 6. Fine as a working reference display, poor for faithful reproduction of fine art.

vendors.name: PPDS (Philips professional displays)
vendors.country: Netherlands-headquartered global operation; Philips professional display brand licensee
vendors.corporate_form: Corporate business unit operating the Philips professional display brand
vendors.ownership: Operates the Philips brand for professional displays under licence. The parent relationship (TP Vision / TPV Technology) was not verified in this session and is recorded as INFERENCE.
vendors.funding: N/A - corporate business unit
vendors.revenue_scale: Not disclosed in the material retrieved
vendors.hardware_track_record: Established category leader in e-paper signage and the first mover at both sizes. Introduced the 25 in Philips Tableaux at ISE 2023 as, by its own account, the world's first full-size full-colour digital signage display of its type, then the 32 in Tableaux 5150I as the world's first signage display confirmed on E Ink Spectra 6 - a claim corroborated by E Ink CEO Johnson Lee, who is quoted confirming PPDS as the first implementer of the 31.5 in module. Named on E Ink's own Spectra 6 brand page as a customer. Maintains a 24x7 pre- and post-sales technical support team, an AV distribution channel, an Android SoC platform family shared across products, and its own PPDS Wave cloud management platform while explicitly supporting third-party management software. Documented product lifecycle from announcement through ISE and InfoComm demonstrations to shipping product.
vendors.abandonment_history: None found. The Tableaux range has been extended rather than dropped - the 25 in was followed by the 32 in, and the range is documented as multi-award-winning with installations across education, retail, corporate, transportation, hospitality, food and beverage and public venues.
vendors.rationale: Rated medium, and would be higher with verified corporate financials. The evidence for durability is behavioural rather than financial and is quite strong: this is a professional AV manufacturer with a named product series it has extended over multiple generations, a 24x7 support organisation, channel distribution, a shared Android SoC platform across its portfolio, deployed installations across many verticals, and a confirmed first-implementer relationship with E Ink at both 25 in and 31.5 in. That is an organisation with continuity obligations to integrators, which is a materially different risk posture from a crowdfunding startup. Rated medium rather than high only because ownership, revenue and headcount could not be verified, and because it depends on a brand licence rather than owning the Philips brand outright. FOR THIS CLIENT: PPDS is the best combination of durability and plausible programmability among established vendors - Android SoC, 16 GB storage, five independent local content paths (USB, micro USB, Micro SD, LAN, Wi-Fi 5), PoE, and explicit support for third-party rather than vendor-only management software. The blockers are 93 PPI, 16:9 landscape geometry, signage aesthetics, channel-only purchase and no published API or SDK.

vendors.name: PPDS / TP Vision / MMD (TPV Technology — Philips professional display licensee)
vendors.country: Philips brand is Dutch; TPV Technology is Taiwanese in origin and Chinese-controlled today
vendors.corporate_form: Public company. TPV Technology Co., Ltd, listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange as 000727. PPDS is the trading name for Philips professional displays, operated through TP Vision Europe B.V. and MMD-Monitors & Displays Nederland B.V.
vendors.ownership: THE STRUCTURAL POINT HE SHOULD UNDERSTAND: the Philips display business is a BRAND LICENCE, not ownership. Koninklijke Philips owns the trademark and licenses it; TPV holds exclusive worldwide rights to operate Philips-branded monitor, TV and audio/video products, with Philips taking revenue-based royalties. Largest shareholder is Nanjing CEC Panda Information Industry Group with 24.51%. TPV was dual-listed in Hong Kong and Singapore, privatised at the end of 2019, then relisted in mainland China by end-2020 via a material asset restructuring with Nanjing Huadong Electronics Information & Technology (a Shenzhen-listed company under the same controlling shareholder), renaming to TPV Technology Co., Ltd in May 2021.
vendors.funding: Not applicable — established listed manufacturer
vendors.public_ticker: 000727 (Shenzhen Stock Exchange). Formerly HK 0903 and a Singapore listing, both withdrawn on privatisation at end-2019.
vendors.revenue_scale: Annual revenue exceeding RMB 50 billion in recent years, with annual output of around 50 million units across 11 manufacturing bases. Monitor division has been world number one for 21 consecutive years at roughly 30% market share; TVs consistently in the global top 10.
vendors.headcount: Approximately 3,000 R&D engineers; over 3,500 sales and service centres globally. Total headcount not stated.
vendors.hardware_track_record: Very long. Origins as Admiral Overseas Corporation, founded in Taiwan in 1967, renamed TPV Technology Limited in 2000 — 59 years. More than 1,000 patents. Owns AOC, AGON and Envision outright alongside the Philips licence. For e-paper specifically: PPDS/Philips is a NAMED PARTNER in E Ink's own ecosystem listing, and Tableaux now spans two generations — the 25in ACeP model (2023) and the 32in Spectra 6 5150I (announced Nov 2023, shown ISE 2024) — with full published datasheets and a 3-year warranty.
vendors.abandonment_history: None found for the Tableaux line, and the licence structure has been consolidating rather than eroding: PPDS US became a wholly-owned TPV Group subsidiary effective 1 May 2022, moving off a prior third-party arrangement to get direct access to TPV manufacturing and priority component allocation. No news of licence loss, dispute or non-renewal. The unquantified risk is that NO SOURCE I fetched discloses the licence term, expiry or renewal conditions — the original 2008 transfer announcement does not state a duration.
vendors.rationale: A 59-year-old manufacturer with RMB 50bn+ revenue, 50 million units a year, 11 plants, #1 in monitors for 21 consecutive years at ~30% share, 3,000 R&D engineers, a listed vehicle and a state-linked anchor shareholder. Corporate survival is not the worry, and the consolidation of PPDS US into TPV in 2022 shows commitment rather than retreat. The one named dependency is real but bounded: the Philips brand is rented on terms whose duration is not public. For his purposes the more relevant durability point is favourable — Tableaux is an Android device with local Ethernet, USB and microSD, so a brand or vendor discontinuity would not brick it.

vendors.hardware_track_record: Decades in professional and consumer displays. E-paper specifically: the 25in Philips Tableaux debuted at ISE 2023; the 32in Philips Tableaux 5150I on E Ink Spectra 6 (2560x1440, about 65,000 colours, zero power for static images, Android SoC, PoE, PPDS Wave CMS) was announced for ISE 2024 in Barcelona. The catch is that it is digital signage, not an art frame: no battery, PoE or mains power, industrial styling, quote-only pricing, and a CMS-shaped content workflow. For a client whose priority is a display his own app can drive and that will still work in 2029, this deserves a serious look even though it will never look like a picture frame. A Lloyds Bank PLC charge from 2020-09-27 also remains outstanding. Then on 2026-01-01 a CEO TRANSITION: co-founder Robert Bicket moved to Chief Strategy & Partnerships Officer and COO David Barker became CEO, framed as the 'next phase of growth and global expansion'.

vendors.rationale: Papercast is the real thing on engineering — proprietary driver board, its own firmware, a 55-country transit installed base, and no filing delinquency in nine years. But the October 2025 transaction is a yellow flag the client should not wave past: both founders' controlling stakes were extinguished, pre-emption rights were stripped, and the incoming director simultaneously took a fixed and floating charge over the company's property IN HIS PERSONAL NAME, on top of a bank charge still outstanding. That structure is what a rescue or a hard-terms growth financing looks like, not a clean equity round — and the CEO handover came eight weeks later. Combined with entirely undisclosed revenue at this scale, this is medium rather than higher. If the client seriously considers the 32in unit, ask for the FY2025 accounts and the Bake charge instrument first. Note also the panel is MONOCHROME greyscale, so it fails the colour-art requirement regardless.

vendors.name: PocketBook International SA (InkPoster)
vendors.corporate_form: Privately held S.A. Legal identity confirmed against a regulatory filing: FCC grantee code 2AUVW is 'Pocketbook International SA., Crocicchio Cortogna, 6, 6900 Lugano, Switzerland', and inkposter.com's own About page names the same entity.
vendors.ownership: Private; owners not disclosed. Notably an ACQUIRER rather than a target — became a substantial shareholder and co-owner of Bigme in May 2024, its first considerable acquisition since it began releasing e-readers in 2012.
vendors.funding: No rounds found; self-funded and trade-financed.
vendors.revenue_scale: USD 151 million (2010) — the only revenue figure I could source, and badly dated. Nothing more recent. Manufacturing partner is Foxconn.
vendors.hardware_track_record: Founded 2007 in Kyiv, HQ relocated to Lugano in 2012 — about 19 years. Continuous product line from the PocketBook 301 (2008) through the world's first colour E Ink e-reader with built-in light (Color Lux, 2013), water-resistant and camera models (2014), Kaleido colour (2020) and audiobook/advanced-colour devices (2022-2024). THE HARDEST CONTINUITY EVIDENCE IN THIS SURVEY: 24 FCC ID applications under grantee 2AUVW spanning 2019-11-27 to 2026-05-20, with no gap year — an independently auditable record of unbroken engineering throughput. Products sold in 35 countries across Central, Eastern and Western Europe, the Baltics, CIS, Australia, Israel and New Zealand; 30+ localised country sites; sells via Amazon.
vendors.abandonment_history: None found; but the InkPoster line is under a year old, which is itself the risk, and there is no firmware-support history to judge. A second signal I found directly and should flag: as of 2026-08 EVERY InkPoster model on inkposter.com is either 'Sold out' or 'Notify me' — including the 31.5in and 28.5in that were on sale from December 2025, and the Duna 40.5in that coverage said would ship April 2026 and still is not purchasable. That is either strong demand or supply/production difficulty; I cannot tell which, and he should not assume the benign reading.
vendors.rationale: PocketBook the company is genuinely durable — 19 years, a Swiss S.A., Foxconn manufacturing, 35 countries, an unbroken 24-filing FCC trail through May 2026, and the cash to buy into Bigme. On the company alone this would be high. It is held at medium because InkPoster specifically is an ~18-month-old venture into a new category whose flagship sizes depend on a Sharp IGZO plus E Ink Spectra 6 stack neither PocketBook nor its customers control, whose pricing is incoherent (the 28.5in costs $700 more than the larger 31.5in), and whose entire range is currently unbuyable. For his purposes the vendor rating is nearly irrelevant anyway, because the integration is closed: with no API, no local push and no SD/USB path, an InkPoster is only as useful as PocketBook's app and service, so vendor risk and product risk collapse into the same risk. That coupling is precisely what he should avoid.

Also distributes through Archiproducts, an architect/design channel.
vendors.abandonment_history: MIXED, WITH REAL BLACK MARKS — AND ONE THAT IS EASY TO MISREAD. (1) In November 2012 PocketBook ABANDONED THE US MARKET ENTIRELY: closed its Kansas HQ and all retail and popup stores including New York, replaced its CEO, cut new-reader development, and left US customers with effectively no customer service. The trade article covering it predicted the company would be dead by late 2013 — it was wrong by thirteen years. Read this as a survived near-death event AND as proven willingness to abandon a whole region overnight, not as current condition. (2) The PocketBook CAD Reader, announced 2013, never shipped — vaporware. (3) The planned Viva Gallery 3 e-reader slipped repeatedly through the year before E Ink deprioritised the panel generation. (4) PocketBook Cloud suffered an HTTP 502 outage 2023-12-23 to 25, about two days, with no public post-mortem — minor, but the sync service is a real dependency. (5) The flagship Tela 40.5 has been shown at CES and priced but was still 'Notify me' (not purchasable) on PocketBook's own US store when fetched 2026-08-05, roughly seven months after its CES 2026 debut. No insolvency, liquidation or bankruptcy filings; registry status active.
vendors.distributor_footprint: PocketBook: 32-40 countries, 130 service centres, established European retail, own US and EU stores, 2-year EU warranty, Archiproducts design channel. IMPORTANT GAP: I could not verify a single NAMED authorised retailer — both 'Where to buy' pages are JavaScript maps that returned no dealer names, and no Amazon or B&H presence was confirmed for InkPoster.
vendors.acquisitions: ACQUIRER, NOT TARGET, AND THE CONSOLIDATOR OF THIS CATEGORY. Became a substantial shareholder and co-owner of Bigme on 2024-05-25, with active cross-sharing of R&D teams; the first fruit was the PocketBook InkPad EO, PocketBook firmware on Bigme InkNote Color+ hardware. Then acquired the Belgian e-paper art-frame maker IONNYK on 2025-09-02, explicitly to gain European production and development capacity and reduce dependence on Asia and the USA, with IONNYK's founders retained.
vendors.rationale: The strongest of the consumer art-frame vendors, and the rating comes almost entirely from the parent rather than the product. A 19-year-old e-reader company with 32-40 country distribution, a Foxconn line, a 2-year EU warranty and named partnerships with both E Ink and Sharp is a fundamentally different counterparty from a Kickstarter brand — it has an installed base to protect and a supply relationship deep enough to secure a Sharp IGZO backplane, which no crowdfunded competitor has. AND THE CLIENT SHOULD UNDERSTAND THE CONCENTRATION HE IS BUYING: PocketBook now owns InkPoster, owns IONNYK, and co-owns Bigme. Three of the apparently independent options in this survey are the same counterparty. That is concentration risk dressed up as choice, and it also means a single PocketBook stumble takes out a large fraction of the credible field. Not rated high because: the Swiss entity is a CHF 100,000 shell with one administrator and no filed accounts, so the group's current financial condition is genuinely unknown and the unverified $151m-to-$11m revenue signal is worrying; there is a documented pattern of announcing e-paper products that slip or never ship (Viva, CAD Reader) and the flagship Tela 40.5 is itself still unpurchasable months after launch; the InkPoster line is only about a year old with no track record of long-term firmware support for THIS family; and no named retail partner could be verified. Practical advice: buy the 28.5in or 31.5in that actually ships rather than betting on the 40.5in, and get local-transfer capability confirmed in writing first.

vendors.name: Sony Group Corporation (cautionary precedent, no longer a vendor)
vendors.corporate_form: Public company (Tokyo and New York listings)
vendors.ownership: Publicly held
vendors.funding: n/a
vendors.revenue_scale: One of the world's largest consumer-electronics groups; not quantified here because it is a precedent, not a candidate.
vendors.hardware_track_record: Sony shipped the 13.3in DPT-S1 and then the DPT-RP1 Digital Paper (13.3in E Ink Carta, 2200x1650, 207 PPI, launched 2017) plus the 10.3in DPT-CP1 — for years the reference large-format e-paper device.
vendors.abandonment_history: THE MOST IMPORTANT ABANDONMENT PRECEDENT IN THIS SURVEY. By August 2020 the DPT-RP1 and DPT-CP1 were discontinued and no longer sold through distribution partners including Amazon, B&H and Adorama. Sony's US Digital Paper division CLOSED ENTIRELY; the Digital Paper landing page was REMOVED from Sony's website, leaving only accessories (cases, nibs, styli) marketed. The leadership behind the product left in 2018 and 2019, and Sony ended its marketing agency relationship in early 2020. Sony pivoted to bulk deals and white-label supply to third parties such as Fujitsu rather than selling the device itself; firmware and the desktop app were maintained out of Sony Japan rather than the US.
vendors.distributor_footprint: Withdrawn
vendors.rationale: Included deliberately, and the client should read it as the governing lesson of this whole file. Sony was — and is — one of the largest, best-capitalised consumer-electronics companies on earth. It had the strongest large-format e-paper product in the market. It killed the line, shut the division, deleted the product page, let the responsible executives leave, and pivoted to white-labelling, all inside about three years of the DPT-RP1's launch. A VENDOR'S BALANCE SHEET TELLS YOU WHETHER THE COMPANY WILL SURVIVE; IT TELLS YOU ALMOST NOTHING ABOUT WHETHER THE PRODUCT LINE WILL. So corporate staying power is necessary but not sufficient, and the real protection is architectural: a device whose images arrive over a documented local interface (USB, SD, HDMI, local network push) keeps working when the vendor loses interest, whereas a device that depends on a vendor app, cloud or subscription becomes a dead panel the day the vendor reprioritises. Weight integration openness at least as heavily as vendor size.

vendors.name: SwitchBot (Woan Technology (Shenzhen) Co., Ltd.)
vendors.country: China (Shenzhen), with a reported Cayman holding structure and a Hong Kong listing application
vendors.corporate_form: Private, venture-backed, with a Hong Kong IPO application filed June 2025. Reported structure: a Cayman holding company over the Chinese operating entity Woan Technology (Shenzhen) Co., Ltd.; earlier product listings used the name Wonderlabs, Inc.
vendors.ownership: Founder-led (Li Zhichen and Pan Yang, Harbin Institute of Technology alumni) plus institutional venture investors
vendors.funding: THE BEST-DOCUMENTED FUNDING HISTORY OF ANY CONSUMER FRAME VENDOR HERE. Founded 2015. Pre-A and Series A in 2018. 2021: RMB 128 million (about US$17.6 million) from Source Code Capital, Yintai Capital and Hillhouse Capital. March 2022: Series B+ of RMB 200 million (about US$27.5 million) from Fortune Capital and SDIC Innovation. May 2025: RMB 70 million (about US$9.6 million) from Brizan Ventures at a valuation of RMB 4.05 billion (about US$555 million). Ventech China also appears as an investor (unverified).
vendors.revenue_scale: Not disclosed in absolute terms. 2024 geographic mix: over 95% of revenue international — Japan 57.7%, Europe 21.4%, North America 15.9%. A RMB 4.05 billion valuation implies real scale.
vendors.hardware_track_record: About 11 years, and crucially a record of shipping MANY products rather than one: SwitchBot Bot (the finger robot) in 2017, SwitchBot Curtain in 2020, a broad smart-home ecosystem since, now extending into embodied AI robotics. The AI Art Frame is a 2026 line extension into e-paper at 7.3in ($149.99), 13.3in ($349.99) and 31.5in ($1,299.99) on E Ink Spectra 6 with a 2,000 mAh battery rated up to two years.
vendors.abandonment_history: Not researched to conclusion — a genuine gap. What the fetched evidence does establish is that the COMMERCIAL MODEL ITSELF CREATES ABANDONMENT EXPOSURE: the AI Art Frame's headline feature is AI generation delivered as a $3.99/month subscription after a 30-day trial, and the app holds only 10 locally-stored images. A subscription service is something a company can switch off, and a 10-image local cache is not a substitute for a local delivery path. If the IPO fails or the frame line underperforms, the AI service is the first thing to go and the buyer keeps whatever the app still does offline.
vendors.distributor_footprint: Own regional storefronts plus broad third-party retail. Japan is its largest market at 57.7% of 2024 revenue, Europe 21.4%, North America 15.9%.
vendors.rationale: On pure financial backing this is the second-strongest consumer vendor after PocketBook and arguably better capitalised: four disclosed rounds from named institutional investors (Hillhouse, Source Code, Fortune Capital, SDIC Innovation, Brizan, Ventech China), a RMB 4.05bn valuation, an 11-year multi-product hardware record, and a filed Hong Kong listing application. This is NOT a one-product startup. Two things hold it at medium. First, an IPO application is not an IPO, and a pre-profit consumer-hardware company in a crowded smart-home market is exactly the profile that gets recapitalised or restructured. Second and more decision-relevant: SwitchBot is a smart-home ecosystem company for which the art frame is one SKU among dozens. Its incentive is to keep the app and subscription alive, not to guarantee a decade of firmware for a $1,299 frame — and when smart-home companies prune, they prune SKUs. The 31.5in unit is also only about 93-PPI-class for its size and its content path is app-and-cloud-shaped, which is the wrong architecture for a self-hosted pipeline.

vendors.name: Visionect d.o.o.
vendors.corporate_form: d.o.o. — Slovenian private limited company. Full legal name 'VISIONECT, svetovanje in tehnološke rešitve d.o.o.', registered Ljubljana; reg. no. 2333988000, VAT SI 91272149. Classed a medium-sized enterprise.
vendors.ownership: Private, founder- and management-held: Zalar Rok 15.84%, Birsa Luka 15.84%, Rodij (investment company) 8.00%, Stele Jaka 6.41%, Furlan Vladimir 2.57%, with STH Ventures holding the remainder. IMPORTANT: the registry record lists STH Ventures as IN LIQUIDATION — a shareholder in liquidation can force a stake sale, so treat the cap table as potentially unstable. Also operates the 'Joan' brand (getjoan.com), which is not a separate legal entity.
vendors.funding: No priced VC round found. STH Ventures is an investor (stake, date and amount undisclosed) alongside the small Rodij holding. Website footer carries EU co-funding and ministry acknowledgements, indicating grant support.
vendors.revenue_scale: THE BEST-VERIFIED FINANCIALS IN THIS SURVEY, because Slovenia publishes filed accounts. Revenue 2021 EUR 4,932,237 → 2022 EUR 7,087,004 → 2023 EUR 8,471,524 (72% growth over two years). Net result 2021 −EUR 1,465,102 → 2022 −EUR 426,095 → 2023 +EUR 513,114 — a genuine turn to profit. Total assets 2023 EUR 4.59m.
vendors.hardware_track_record: Founded 2007-10-11, so about 19 years as a company and roughly 12 shipping e-paper hardware. Focused B2B specialist with a coherent product family (Place & Play 6in, 13in, 32in) plus the Joan room-booking and visitor-management line, its own Software Suite, published REST API documentation, a maintained Docker distribution (100K+ pulls, updated within the last month), and a GitHub organisation with vendor-published client code. Enterprise customer logos include Sony, Dell, Samsung, Microsoft, Cisco, Siemens, Amazon, NASA and IKEA. Formal partner and affiliate programmes; distributed through AV integrators and listed in E Ink's own kit shop. Credit rating A+ (2024), VAT-registered, no tax arrears, no blocked accounts — though the detailed assessment is 'lower-middle: stable operations containing certain risk factors'.
vendors.abandonment_history: DOCUMENTED, DATED AND MATERIAL — THIS COMPANY HAS ALREADY DONE THE EXACT THING THE CLIENT FEARS. (1) ON-PREMISE DEPLOYMENT KILLED: 'As of January 1, 2023, the on-premise service is no longer supported' and 'We will stop further development and new software releases... no updates can be expected after the year 2023.' Customers declining migration own their own security updates, lose new features, and Visionect states it CANNOT GUARANTEE DEVICES WILL CONTINUE TO OPERATE with an on-premise VM. New devices (Joan 6 Pro) are CLOUD-ONLY. (2) FIRST-GENERATION HARDWARE DROPPED: support for first-gen 9.7in and 6in Signs ended at Software Suite 3.0, and connecting one to a 3.0+ Suite shows a notice to revert to the 2.x series. (3) Numerous other removals: armhf 32-bit ARM build removed in 7.0; PV2 protocol disabled 7.9.0 and removed with old PV3 in 8.0.0; cookiefs removed 7.0; Storage component removed 4.2.0; session pre-loading removed 3.0; hourly display updates removed 5.2.3; Virtual Screens temporarily removed 4.0.0. Current Suite 8.3.1. (4) Earlier product abandonments by their own account: e-paper retail price labels (dropped to competition) and 'Geoffrey' restaurant menus (dropped despite success). (5) A 2020 business-model shift away from hardware-led to end-to-end solutions. (6) February 2026 at ISE 2026: REBRANDED TO JOAN WORKPLACE AND WENT SOFTWARE-FIRST — but explicitly NOT discontinuing hardware, 'continues to double down on its signature monochrome e-paper aesthetic, with new form factors and gadgets on the roadmap'. Platform now also supports third-party LCD and e-paper displays and coexists with Crestron.
vendors.rationale: Say it plainly: an EUR 8.5m-revenue, ~47-person Slovenian private company that lost money in two of its last three filed years is not a durable institution, and one of its shareholders is in liquidation. What raises it to medium rather than low is unusually good evidence of a real, improving business: 19 years old, 72% revenue growth 2021-23, a genuine swing to profit in 2023, headcount up 34 to 47, an A+ credit rating with no tax or account distress, blue-chip logos, integrator distribution, an E Ink shop listing, and a Docker image with 100K+ pulls updated within the month. BUT I MUST CORRECT MY FIRST-PASS REASONING HERE. I had assumed the self-hosted architecture meant a Visionect insolvency would leave him with a working local server. It would not: Visionect's own installation docs say devices 'will not be able to operate' without a valid VSS_LICENSE_ID, so if the company folds or simply declines to renew, the displays stop — on his hardware, on his server, in his house. That converts Visionect from 'small but architecturally safe' into 'small vendor holding a remote kill switch', which for a 3-year horizon is materially worse than the financials alone suggest. Combined with a monochrome panel that the one independent hands-on reviewer called outdated and low-contrast, I would not build on Visionect unless the licence terms can be pinned down in writing first.

vendors.country: Norway (Oslo). Manufacturing in China and Vietnam; distribution hubs Hong Kong, Mexico, Netherlands, US.

vendors.ownership: Private, founder-and-employee majority, with Spark Capital and later international minority investors.
vendors.funding: Series A US$15 million from Spark Capital, October 2019 (Spark remains a shareholder). A further minority-stake round from international investors closed 2021 and was announced May 2022 at a valuation above US$1 billion. SEPARATELY AND IMPORTANTLY, THERE IS A LISTED DEBT INSTRUMENT: a NOK 500 million senior secured floating-rate bond on the Oslo Stock Exchange, ISIN NO0013030205, coupon 3-month NIBOR + 7.00% per annum, issued 2023-10-12, MATURING 2027-10-12.
vendors.public_ticker: No equity listing. Bond ISIN NO0013030205 on the Oslo Stock Exchange.
vendors.revenue_scale: By far the largest and most transparent business in the device set: US$303 million in 2021 (+120% YoY, US$31 million EBITDA); US$434.3 million revenue and US$24.7 million NET PROFIT in 2024; about 791,000 units sold in 2024; 568,000 paying Connect subscribers. It is the only vendor here with mandatory public financial disclosure, which exists precisely because of the bond.
vendors.headcount: TRAJECTORY IS THE STORY: 300+ (2022) to 500+ (2024) to 580, then down to 500 in a first cut around August 2025, then to about 300 after a second cut of 200-plus announced 2026-04-22 to 26. Roughly a 40% reduction inside eight months.
vendors.hardware_track_record: About 9 years, and none of it abandoned: reMarkable 1 (August 2017), reMarkable 2 (March 2020), Type Folio (March 2023), Paper Pro 11.8in (September 2024), Paper Pro Move 7.3in (September 2025). Connect subscription launched October 2021 and is still running with 568k subscribers. LARGEST DEVICE EVER SHIPPED IS 11.8IN, AND THE STRATEGY IS EXPLICITLY MOVING SMALLER — the 2025 follow-up went DOWN to 7.3in, with the roadmap shifting toward portability plus AI and cloud workflow features. Nothing above 15in exists or is planned.
vendors.abandonment_history: No product or firmware abandonment found — the line is short and all of it is still supported, which is a genuinely good record. Documented friction is customer-service-shaped rather than abandonment-shaped: Trustpilot complaints cluster on warranty claims, replacement logistics and subscription billing, and the standard warranty is only 1 year with extended coverage sold via Connect. THE REAL RISK IS FINANCIAL AND VERY CONCRETE: leadership churn (CEO Philip Hess out after about two years, replaced by Vegard Gullaksen Veiteberg, previously interim), with chairman Marius Juul Molle on the record that 'There is a tougher macro picture and global unrest. We have noticed weaker demand and thus falling sales.' Additional cited pressures: memory-chip price inflation driven by AI demand, and Amazon's Kindle Scribe outselling reMarkable significantly.
vendors.distributor_footprint: Global direct-to-consumer plus retail; the most mature consumer operation in the set.
vendors.rationale: OUT OF SCOPE ON SIZE — largest device is 11.8in and the product strategy is deliberately going smaller — but included because it is the most instructive financial case in the survey. reMarkable is the ONLY vendor here with audited public financials, real profitability, and roughly 800,000 units a year. And it has just cut about 40% of its workforce, replaced its CEO, and carries a NOK 500 million bond at NIBOR+700bp MATURING IN OCTOBER 2027 — inside the client's three-year window. Refinancing that against weaker demand is the single most concrete, publicly documented financial risk event anywhere in this vendor set, and it exists in the file only because reMarkable is obliged to disclose. Every other vendor here has risks of the same or greater magnitude that are simply invisible. That is the lesson: absence of bad financial news among private vendors is absence of disclosure, not absence of risk.

leads_not_followed.what: ANSWERED DURING THIS SURVEY, recorded here as the headline result: the Samsung EM32DX is locally driveable over MDC on TCP 1515 with no cloud and no app. What remains open is the exact byte-level content mechanism and its durability
leads_not_followed.why_promising: I opened this as the survey's biggest unknown and closed it. Two independent repos confirm the capability (vgavro/samsung-mdc, 109 stars, explicitly listing EM32DX; WeeJeWel/node-samsung-emdx, a one-line show-image CLI stated to work without cloud or app). What I did NOT verify first-hand is the mechanism detail reported from the upstream issue threads — a content.json whose image_url points at the user's own local HTTP server, a sub-256-byte URL limit, and a requirement that the content UUID change on every update or the panel will not refresh. Worth reading vgavro/samsung-mdc issues #20, #21, #22 and #24 before writing code, and worth checking whether Samsung firmware updates preserve the behaviour, since Samsung does not document it.

leads_not_followed.what: Whether the reverse-engineered Visionect PV3 device protocol server (timeframe/ha-addon) can be extended from the 13in Place & Play to the 32in — which would remove the licence kill switch entirely
leads_not_followed.why_promising: This is the one lead that could rescue Visionect. Its REST API is the best-documented integration in the survey, but a self-hosted VSS stops working without a valid VSS_LICENSE_ID, which is a remote kill switch held by a 47-person company. timeframe/ha-addon already contains a clean-room TCP server implementing the device wire protocol on port 11114, with a documented 20-byte header, a 4bpp/16-level greyscale LZ4 strip encoder, and even an MITM proxy used to derive it — but it is written for 1600x1200 13in panels. Extending the encoder to the 32in's 2560x1440 would give licence-free operation on hardware he owns. Non-trivial but bounded, and the hard protocol work is already done and published.

leads_not_followed.what: LARGELY ANSWERED: ADB works on the Tableaux platform. What remains is confirming APK install (not just file push) on the 25.3in and 32in specifically, and whether network ADB works or a USB cable is always required
leads_not_followed.why_promising: A hobbyist has verifiably pushed image files onto a Tableaux over `adb push` into /storage/emulated/0/Pictures/ and driven it with scrcpy, and four commercial CMS vendors integrate by sideloading their own APK — so the platform is open. Two gaps remain. First, `adb install` on the 25.3in/32in is reported from a CMS vendor's certified-device guide that I did not fetch myself. Second, NO source shows network ADB (adb connect <ip>:5555) on any Philips signage display; every example uses USB, so provisioning may need physical access — fine for one-time setup, awkward if he wants remote recovery. Also worth an empirical test: whether SICP responds on TCP 5000 (`nc <ip> 5000`), since the SICP spec lists no ePaper model and neither Tableaux manual mentions it — though SICP is control-only and would not carry images anyway.

leads_not_followed.what: The resolution and PPI of the E Ink 25.3in Spectra 6 module (ED2208-PEA, in stock at $1,400), AND whether any TCON or controller exists that a non-specialist could use to drive a Mini-LVDS 25.3in panel
leads_not_followed.why_promising: No finished product pairs Spectra 6 colour with a 25.3in high-PPI panel — the shipping Spectra 6 devices are all 93 PPI 31.5in units, while the 145 PPI 25.3in devices are all lower-quality Kaleido or older ACeP. If this module is 3200x1800 it would be the best fine-art e-paper surface in existence. TWO THINGS TO CORRECT FROM MY FIRST PASS, both of which make this harder than it looked: the E Ink listing does not publish resolution at all, and 25.3in panels use Mini-LVDS requiring a TCON or FPGA, so the Modos Glider pairing I initially suggested is not viable (Glider tops out around 224 MP/s versus the 364 MP/s a 25.3in 3200x1800 needs at 60Hz). Ask E Ink for both the datasheet AND what its 'Vision Driving Board' actually supports — that board is the only named controller path and I could not find any documentation for it.

leads_not_followed.what: CORRECTION WORTH PROPAGATING: the widely-repeated claim that Modos Glider drives 4in-42in e-paper panels is false, and there is currently NO open-source controller for any panel over 15 inches
leads_not_followed.why_promising: Recorded as a lead because the error is in press coverage and will keep resurfacing. The '4 to 42 inch' range comes from an appendix Screen List in Glider's README that carries an explicit disclaimer — 'This is a list of all E-ink screens that have public information available, not a list of screens that's compatible with the Glider' — and the largest panel marked Tested there is 5.0in, with the compatibility table topping out at 13.3in. The bandwidth ceilings confirm it. Separately, epdiy (1.9k stars) supports nothing above 13.3in, ESPHome's waveshare_epaper caps at 13.3in mono / 7.3in colour, and Inkplate's largest is 13.3in. The practical consequence: the ONLY >15in self-build route today is the QSPI 31.5in Spectra 6 panel with Good Display's own ESP32-S3 kit. If he wants a bare-panel build, that is the one to buy.

leads_not_followed.what: ANSWERED AND IT IS BAD NEWS: a lapsed Visionect licence stops the devices working even on a self-hosted server. What remains open is the current price and whether any perpetual option exists
leads_not_followed.why_promising: I opened this as the question standing between Visionect's excellent API and a clean recommendation, and the answer disqualifies it for most purposes. Visionect's installation docs state 'The VSS_LICENSE_ID environmental variable must be set in order for the VSS to function. Without a proper value for the license, the devices will not be able to operate.' A developer who deployed them reports the on-premise fee arrived around 2021 at $7/month per device after years of being free. visionect.com/pricing returns HTTP 404, so the current figure is unknown — ask Visionect directly for the Essential plan price, the term, and whether a perpetual licence exists, and note that a shareholder (STH Ventures) is in liquidation.

leads_not_followed.what: Samsung Color E-Paper 25-inch (3200x1800) — is it actually purchasable anywhere?
leads_not_followed.why_promising: SIGNIFICANT and I could not close it. Samsung's ISE 2025 announcement listed a 25in at 3200x1800 alongside the 13in, 32in and 75in — that is Spectra-class colour at 145 PPI, the combination that would make Samsung both the safest vendor AND the best art panel. But it is absent from the US and Hong Kong storefronts I fetched, and samsung.com/us/business/smart-signage/e-paper/ returned a page with no e-paper SKUs listed at all. My WebSearch budget (200 calls) was exhausted before I could sweep for regional listings. If a 25in EMDX exists to buy, it changes the shortlist.

leads_not_followed.what: Bigme B251 (non-Pro) 25.3in all-in-one monitor-and-PC with an onboard operating system
leads_not_followed.why_promising: Bigme sells a 25.3in colour e-ink device that is a complete computer rather than a monitor. If its onboard OS is Android or Linux and permits installing software, it would be a single-box solution — his renderer running on the display itself, no attached host, no cloud. I did not fetch the product page for this variant, so I have no verified specs, OS or price.

leads_not_followed.what: E Ink's own 75-inch Spectra 6 colour ePaper display, and Samsung's 75in 5K EMDX
leads_not_followed.why_promising: Both are outside my 'purchasable today' slice but bear on the 3-year view. E Ink's news index references a 75in Spectra 6 launch, and Samsung demonstrated a 75in 5K (5120x2880) at ISE 2025 with no announced price or availability. Meanwhile E Ink's H5 production line is now in volume production specifically for 32in and 55in panels, and H6 comes online in 2026 — so large colour panels are the direction of the whole industry, not a niche. A 55in colour panel would likely appear in products within his 3-year window.

leads_not_followed.what: RESOLVED: miractl is real and explicitly supports the Mira Pro 25.3in. No longer a gap
leads_not_followed.why_promising: Recorded only to close it out. The sourcehut URL returned HTTP 502 but github.com/elithper/miractl is live and confirms testing on both the Mira 13.3 and Mira Pro 25.3, controlling refresh mode, speed 1-7, contrast 0-15, dither mode, white/black filters, cool/warm front light and antiflicker, with five presets. Together with mira-js (63 stars), clarkema/miractl (Rust), rynom99/mira-cli and the 854-star timeframe/ha-addon, the BOOX Mira Pro has more independent working tooling than any other device in this survey.

leads_not_followed.what: E Ink kit-store large panels not individually priced: 28in monochrome, 31.2in colour, 31.2in monochrome, 42in monochrome, and 25.3in Kaleido 3
leads_not_followed.why_promising: All appear in E Ink's own developer store inventory alongside the priced 25.3in modules, and the 42in monochrome panel is the largest e-paper surface available to a self-builder anywhere in this survey. Prices and resolutions were not shown on the listing pages I reached; a direct enquiry would open up the large-format self-build option considerably. Note Modos Glider is documented as driving panels up to 42in, so the pairing exists.

leads_not_followed.what: Soofa and MpicoSys — large-format e-paper signage vendors named in the brief's sweep list
leads_not_followed.why_promising: Both were in scope for the commercial/signage category and I reached neither: my WebSearch budget was exhausted at 200 calls first. Soofa in particular sells large solar e-paper community signs. Based on the Papercast and Visionect pattern, expect municipal/B2B sales with a mandatory vendor cloud, but the possibility of a documented API makes them worth a check.

leads_not_followed.what: Independent measurement of Spectra 6 colour accuracy for reproductions — gamut volume, Delta-E, reflectance, bit depth, and whether any vendor publishes an ICC profile
leads_not_followed.why_promising: This is a hole across EVERY device in the survey and it matters specifically for fine art. Not one vendor publishes a colour profile, a gamut volume, a Delta-E figure or a documented dithering approach; E Ink's own Spectra 6 page publishes contrast (30:1) and PPI but no colour metrics at all. Colour-count claims for the very same 31.5in Spectra 6 panel range from 54,600 to 60,000 to 65,000 to 77,000 depending on whose marketing you read. Worse, Samsung and others apply an undocumented device-side 'colour imaging algorithm' to whatever image they receive. For controlled reproduction he needs either measured data or a device where he owns the dithering — which is the strongest single argument for the bare-panel-plus-Glider path.

leads_not_followed.what: Whether Dalian Good Display has any formal standing with E Ink, and who E Ink's authorised Chinese module partners actually are
leads_not_followed.why_promising: Good Display is the practical source for large bare panels and matching controllers, so its film supply matters. I confirmed directly that E Ink's own partner listing does not name Good Display (it names PPDS/Philips, Sharp, AUO Display Plus, MediaTek and others), which suggests Good Display buys on ordinary commercial terms rather than as a partner. A subagent also reports that E Ink's named Chinese partner for flexible/OTFT displays is DKE, and that Good Display operates across at least eight domains with two legal entities sharing one ICP filing — both unverified by me. Worth resolving before designing a product around Good Display part numbers.

leads_not_followed.what: Geniatech direct sales enquiry - request the EPC2530 (25.3", 163 PPI, Android 11) SDK documentation, confirm whether the bundled CMS can be bypassed or self-hosted, whether APK sideloading is permitted, and what MOQ and unit price apply to a single unit
leads_not_followed.why_promising: This is the highest-value unresolved question in the whole slice. Geniatech is the only vendor combining credible corporate durability (27 years, own factory, diversified product lines) with an Android 11 applications processor, an in-house TCON, an explicitly advertised 'Open API & SDK', and the best-resolution large panel available (25.3" at 3200x1800). If the SDK is real and APKs can be sideloaded, this likely beats every consumer frame on both of the client's criteria simultaneously. None of it is published, so it can only be resolved by contacting them.

leads_not_followed.what: BLOOMIN8 local REST API - obtain or reverse-document the full API specification beyond what the Home Assistant component reveals, and confirm image resolution, colour space and dithering requirements for the 28.5" (2160x3060) model
leads_not_followed.why_promising: The BLOOMIN8 28.5" is the best size-plus-openness combination found. Its local HTTP API is real and mDNS-discoverable, but the contract is documented only by vendor-published Home Assistant code plus third-party libraries, not by a specification. For a client pushing gigapixel-derived renders, the exact expected input format and whether upload_dithered_image_data lets him supply his own dithering (rather than accepting the device's) is decisive for colour fidelity. The community CLI mrud/bloomin8-cli explicitly implements Spectra 6 dithering, so the answer is probably recoverable from that code.

leads_not_followed.what: Modos Flow 'Hacking Guide' campaign update (Jul 01, 2026) and the remaining Crowd Supply update series
leads_not_followed.why_promising: Modos published an update titled 'Hacking Guide' on 2026-07-01 plus 'Comparing the Paper Dev Kit with Flow' on 2026-06-18. These are the most likely place to find an authoritative statement on whether the Caster/Glider stack can be brought up on a large Spectra 6 panel and what waveform work that requires - the single biggest open technical question in the open-hardware route. Not read in this session.

leads_not_followed.what: Whether Caster/Glider can render correct COLOUR on a Spectra 6 panel, as opposed to merely driving its LVDS timing
leads_not_followed.why_promising: Glider's documentation states support for panels up to 25.3" and handles the LVDS signalling those panels use, but Caster's stated panel scope is monochrome and colour-filter-array screens. Spectra 6 is a four-pigment microcup system, not a CFA, and needs its own multi-pass waveform set. The open-hardware route to a >15in COLOUR frame hinges entirely on this question and it is currently unresolved - worth raising directly on the Modos Discord/Matrix or in the Caster issue tracker before committing to that path.

leads_not_followed.what: E Ink 'Vision' evaluation kit and Vision Driving Board specifications, plus the rest of E Ink's own driving-board family (HULK, THOR, ICE, Salt, Luvia, CONCERTO, Venus, Scarlet, RedHulk)
leads_not_followed.why_promising: E Ink sells the 31.5" Spectra 6 module directly through its own kit store and names the Vision Driving Board as the companion controller, but publishes neither per-board panel compatibility nor prices on the category listing. This is the manufacturer-sanctioned bare-panel-plus-controller route and is likely the lowest-risk self-build path for correct Spectra 6 colour, since the waveforms come from the panel maker. Individual board product pages were not reached in this session.

leads_not_followed.what: Good Display GDES285E01 (28.5" A2, 2160x3060) full datasheet and its interface type, plus whether a development kit exists for it
leads_not_followed.why_promising: This panel has arguably the best geometry-and-density combination above 15 inches for framed single works (A2 portrait, ~131 PPI), and it is the substrate under both the BLOOMIN8 28.5" and InkPoster Tela 28.5". But Good Display's product page is an unpopulated stub with no interface, dimensions, refresh or price, so a self-build at this size is currently undocumented. The downloadable spec sheet and a direct enquiry to info@good-display.com would settle it.

leads_not_followed.what: Whether the Philips Tableaux 5150I accepts a sideloaded Android APK, and whether PPDS publishes any API or SDK for its Android SoC platform
leads_not_followed.why_promising: Tableaux is the best durability-plus-plausible-programmability combination among established vendors: Android SoC, 16 GB storage, five local content paths, PoE, and explicit support for third-party management software rather than vendor-cloud-only. If APK sideloading is permitted, the client's own app could run on the display itself. The announcement does not state it either way, and no PPDS developer documentation was located.

Their move into Spectra 6 is exactly the kind of new entrant the client asked to have discovered. Not confirmed whether any Aura Ink model exceeds 15 inches, which is the gating question. URLs seen in search results only, not fetched.

leads_not_followed.what: E Ink Marquee panel sizes, resolution and availability timing
leads_not_followed.why_promising: Marquee is E Ink's newest large-area colour platform, introduced at InfoComm 2026 and a Best in Show winner, with a -20 to 65 C range aimed at outdoor DOOH. E Ink has published essentially no specifications. If Marquee brings higher PPI or better colour at large sizes than Spectra 6, it changes the medium-term picture for this client - worth monitoring, though outdoor DOOH positioning suggests coarse pitch.

leads_not_followed.what: Samsung Color E-Paper 75" EMDX availability, price, and whether the Color E-Paper line exposes any API or accepts third-party applications (Tizen/MagicINFO/VXT)

More useful for this client would be establishing whether the shipping 32" EM32DX can be driven by anything other than Samsung's own mobile app - if MagicINFO or a local HTTP path exists, a durable vendor becomes viable. Samsung newsroom pages timed out repeatedly in this session.

leads_not_followed.what: The claim that mass production of the world's first 30-inch-plus colour e-paper display has begun

If the resolution and reflectance are respectable this would break the E Ink single-supply dependency entirely. leads_not_followed.what: Agile (E Ink ecosystem partner) - the 75" Kaleido 3 display and the 'Agile Conversion Engine' middleware
leads_not_followed.why_promising: Agile built a 75" Kaleido 3 display with E Ink and supplies conversion middleware. Kaleido 3 at large size is a different colour technology from Spectra 6 (colour-filter-array over monochrome, faster refresh, lower saturation, higher effective mono resolution), and a middleware layer implies a documented content pipeline. Worth investigating as an alternative colour approach and as a possible source of image-conversion tooling. Named on E Ink's InfoComm page but Agile's own site was not reached.

leads_not_followed.what: Fraimic's local-only mode protocol, and the backers-only campaign updates

If the local mode turns out to be a documented HTTP endpoint rather than a manual browser upload, the 31.5" Large Canvas at USD 1,299 becomes a much stronger candidate than currently rated.

leads_not_followed.what: Whether Visionect has any colour (Spectra 6 or Kaleido) product on its roadmap
leads_not_followed.why_promising: Visionect's self-hosted RESTful JSON API with programmatic control of dithering method and bit-depth encoding is precisely the architecture this client needs, and its Place & Play 32" is in stock at EUR 2,300 - but it is monochrome, which disqualifies it for colour art. A colour Visionect model would immediately become the leading candidate in this entire survey. Worth a direct enquiry.

leads_not_followed.what: Independent measurement of Spectra 6 colour accuracy, gamut and ghosting at large sizes for art reproduction
leads_not_followed.why_promising: The single biggest evidence gap across every device in this slice. Not one vendor documents a colour profile, none publishes measured gamut, and no vendor or reviewer publishes ghosting characterisation for the large panels. All that exists are platform-level marketing figures (4,096 colours, ~85% NTSC, ~30:1 contrast, <=15s full refresh). For an archive of gigapixel scans where reproduction fidelity is the whole point, this needs resolving empirically - most likely by buying one panel or frame and measuring it, since the published record will not answer it.

leads_not_followed.what: Seeed Studio XIAO ePaper DIY Kit EE02 and Soldered Inkplate 13Spectra - 13.3" Spectra 6 open dev boards
leads_not_followed.why_promising: Both are below the 15in floor so they are out of scope as targets, but both are ESP32-S3 open development boards for Spectra 6 colour panels with published toolchains. They are the cheapest way to prototype and validate the client's rendering, dithering and colour-conversion pipeline against real Spectra 6 hardware before committing to an expensive large panel - a genuinely useful de-risking step. URLs seen in search results only, not fetched.

leads_not_followed.what: Whether ANY 2025-2026 crowdfunded frame has actually delivered a unit larger than 15 inches to a backer
leads_not_followed.why_promising: THE HIGHEST-VALUE UNANSWERED QUESTION IN THIS SLICE. Several vendors advertise 25.3in, 28.5in and 31.5in. I found a documented slipped ship date (Fraimic, unconfirmed fulfilment as of 2026-07-27), a dormant storefront seven months post-campaign (InkJoy), and a product absent from its creator's own catalogue (BLOOMIN8) — but NO positive confirmation of large-format delivery from any of them. If none has shipped at size, the entire crowdfunding tier should be excluded from the development-target decision regardless of price. Requires a real browser session against Kickstarter comment threads.

leads_not_followed.what: PocketBook International's current revenue and headcount
leads_not_followed.why_promising: The Swiss entity files no accounts and holds only CHF 100,000 of capital with a single administrator. If true this materially undercuts the medium rating on the group that owns InkPoster AND IONNYK AND co-owns Bigme — i.e. the largest single concentration of credible options in this survey. leads_not_followed.why_promising: Money raised, backer counts, and — critically — the comment threads and creator updates that reveal whether units shipped. Both sites return HTTP 403 to automated fetching, so this needs a real browser.

leads_not_followed.why_promising: Referenced in a June 2019 BusinessWire release that timed out on fetch. Relevant to judging E Ink's own capital discipline.

leads_not_followed.what: BOE Technology's e-paper investment scale, and LG Display / Tianma large-format e-paper programmes
leads_not_followed.why_promising: An industry SEO page claimed BOE has CNY 46 billion committed to e-paper lines targeting IT and signage, credits LG Display with 3.4 million glass sheets of annual capacity and 24-inch smart-city displays, and Tianma with emerging dual-display work. leads_not_followed.what: Electronic shelf label majors as demand-side anchors: VusionGroup (Euronext SESL), Pricer AB (Nasdaq Stockholm), Hanshow
leads_not_followed.why_promising: Not art-frame vendors, but they are why E Ink is profitable and expanding — ESL volumes of 500m units in 2025 heading to 600m in 2026 dwarf the art-frame market entirely. Their health is a leading indicator of E Ink's capex appetite and therefore of large-format panel availability. VusionGroup is partly covered above; Hanshow's own about page returned 404 and Pricer was not reached.

leads_not_followed.what: Sun Vision Display 32in reflective LCD monitor
leads_not_followed.why_promising: The only other >15in reflective-display monitor found (32in colour RLCD, FHD at 60Hz, ambient-light-only, announced 2022-02-05). It is RLCD not electrophoretic e-paper, so a different technology and visual result — but it is the only non-E-Ink reflective large display in the field. No entity, funding, headcount, or evidence it ever shipped.

leads_not_followed.what: Named-but-not-found vendors: Kunkun, Sibrena, 'Ink&Art', 'Artframe', 'Lumina'
leads_not_followed.why_promising: Recorded so they are not re-researched. Kunkun returned only an Indonesian architectural-visualisation studio, an Android app developer and an app launcher — no e-paper frame company. Sibrena returned ZERO results. The others surfaced no matching e-paper frame vendors. These are likely bad leads or mis-transcriptions. Note also that 'Palma' is the Boox Palma, a 6in pocket e-reader, not a frame.
